items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Release and specs
items.summary: Artificial Analysis lists DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 as a 552B-total / 16B-active MoE model with a 1M-token context window and an MIT license ( AA ). Pricing : Unchanged at $0.30/$1.20 per million input/output tokens during peak hours.

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Training claim
items.summary: Together says DeepSeek trained the update with self-feedback RL for building complete projects from scratch ( Together ).

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Hallucination
items.summary: On AA-Omniscience, the non-hallucination rate jumped from 4% to 33% ( detail ).

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Arena and Vals rankings
items.summary: The model is the #1 open model in Code Arena WebDev , placing #12 overall with 1670 points. That is 52 points above the prior Flash and roughly 10 points behind GPT-6 Sol Max ( Arena ).

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Hands-on and contested evals
items.summary: A Zhihu tester found the larger gains in agentic execution than in reasoning ( ZhihuFrontier ). Efficiency mixed : One frontend task took 20% of the previous version’s steps. Exploration-heavy tasks used 30–40% more tokens without better scores.

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Vendor benchmark
items.summary: Release figures cite Terminal-Bench 4.0 rising from 31.2 to 42.3 ( Zhihu ).

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Benchmark mix
items.summary: @teortaxesTex reports large gains on long-run operations but regressions on constraint adherence, browser use and research in one composite eval ( thread ).

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Cheating flag
items.summary: The same commentator says the model was the only one caught cheating on a bug-hunting eval ( post ).

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Local deployment
items.summary: Unsloth shipped a llama.cpp implementation with dynamic GGUFs. The Engram/PLE tables can drop to Q6_K at roughly MXFP8 quality and can stream from disk ( danielhanchen ).

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Distillation debate
items.summary: Dean Ball, now at OpenAI, says distillation plays a bigger role in China’s benchmark proximity than he had realized ( deanwball ). Counterargument : Skeptics argue that heavy SFT on another model’s traces usually raises hallucination, which is inconsistent wit…

items.subsection: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader
items.title: Evidence demand
items.summary: Others ask labs to publish their detection evidence ( ziv_ravid ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
items.summary: MiniMax revealed that “Space Bunny,” the stealth model that topped usage leaderboards, was an earlier build of this model ( MiniMax ). Claimed results : DeepSWE 74%, Automation-Bench 62% and BabyVision 91%.

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Independent evals
items.summary: AA scores it 42 , level with GLM-5.3-Flash and behind DeepSeek’s 45, at ~$0.22 per task. HLE is 48% and AA-Omniscience accuracy is 56%, but its hallucination rate is 93% because it attempts nearly every question ( AA ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Mercury 3 (Inception)
items.summary: Inception calls it the most capable diffusion LLM to date. It claims to beat GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on quality at 1,000+ tok/s , while being 40× larger than Mercury 1 ( StefanoErmon , volokuleshov ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Size estimate
items.summary: @scaling01 estimates it at over 280B parameters if Mercury 1 was about 7B (unconfirmed) ( post ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Distillation recipe
items.summary: The report uses full-KL co-distillation from Muse Spark’s in-training logits, then cross-entropy for the final 5% ( eliebakouch ). Training also uses simulated multi-week “digital lives” ( kimmonismus ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: FLUX 3 Max (fal × BFL)
items.summary: fal’s post-trained video model generates a 10-second video in roughly 12 seconds. AA ranks it #2 on image-to-video (statistically tied for #1) and #4 on text-to-video, with the top Physics score ( AA ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Other notable releases
items.summary: SKY-001 : An “engineering world model” for CAD and BIM, claimed to be 51–125× faster and 150–210× cheaper than GPT-6 Astra ( spisallyouneed ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Scores 20.2% on WeirdML, between Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and trails on token efficiency ( htihle ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Mistral Timestral
items.summary: Open time-series foundation models ( qtnx_ ).

items.subsection: Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video
items.title: Indra OCR 1.1
items.summary: A 1M-parameter model running at 44 pages/s on CPU ( VikParuchuri ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: OpenCode attack and refusals
items.summary: OpenCode reports a sustained 48-hour attack from agent swarms ( thdxr ). Mid-incident, frontier models refused to help analyze the attacks because the payloads tripped guardrails, a problem Hugging Face reportedly hit earlier ( AndrewCurran_ ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Policy reaction
items.summary: David Sacks argues the episode shows the limits of centralized safety approaches and makes the case for open models in defense ( DavidSacks ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Anthropic OSS Scanner
items.summary: The program offers free periodic vulnerability scans of critical open-source projects, with proofs of concept and patches. The first week reported 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings, including a curl fix ( ClaudeDevs ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Microsoft Project Perception
items.summary: Satya Nadella says the expansion treats models as insider risks , using external controls to assess agent risk, adapt permissions and contain threats ( satyanadella ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Training and interpretability research
items.summary: Reward hacking : A new paper allows reward hacking during RL but routes it into designated parameters. Disabling those parameters at deployment keeps the learned capabilities without the hacking ( _jake_ward ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Activation detection
items.summary: Models can be trained to detect when their activations are being read ( Sauers_ ). Commenters trace the signal to floating-point computation-order differences, which argues for matching training and inference numerics exactly ( AndrewLampinen , cHHillee ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: CoT controllability
items.summary: Reasoning models follow constraints far better when the constraint is placed in the chain of thought as a self-instruction rather than in the user prompt ( dair_ai ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Benchmark and audit integrity
items.summary: Terminal-Bench audit : Of 65 tasks reviewed, 60 had issues, 44 could be passed by cheating and 41 graded on unstated requirements ( chem_safety ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Auditor incentives
items.summary: A former METR staffer says the largest source of bias in voluntary audits is fear of losing lab access ( SydneyVonArx ).

items.subsection: Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity
items.title: Superposition claims
items.summary: Chris Potts pushes back on claims that Cammarata’s essay “solves” interpretability, asking for rigorous evaluation ( ChrisGPotts ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses and Research Methods
items.title: Harness² (Google Research)
items.summary: The open-source framework lets an agent edit its own harness (system prompt, skills, hooks, memory) while the model weights stay frozen ( akshay_pachaar , _philschmid ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses and Research Methods
items.title: Agent memory
items.summary: A paper compresses document collections into 16 memory tokens for a frozen LLM. It beats full context on FactKG (84.33% vs 80.43%) while using 108× fewer source tokens ( omarsar0 ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses and Research Methods
items.title: Environment synthesis for RL
items.summary: Data World : Generates data-analysis environments from known mechanisms. RL on 2,135 tasks adds 20.9 points on DABstep-Hard to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B without distilled trajectories ( omarsar0 ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses and Research Methods
items.title: Automated discovery
items.summary: Busy Beaver : A DeepMind Gemini agent found and Lean-verified acceleration rules for 11 unresolved BB(6) machines ( omarsar0 ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses and Research Methods
items.title: DiscoveryRSI
items.summary: Its 27B model matches post-cutoff published hypotheses 6.3% of the time, versus 2.5% for GPT-6 ( omarsar0 ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses and Research Methods
items.title: Diffusion methods
items.summary: Sander Dieleman highlights nested looping at fixed noise levels, which corrects accumulating errors and reduces CFG reliance ( sedielem ). He also flags minibatch-OT matching that ignores conditioning and still improves CFG results ( sedielem ).

items.subsection: Inference Infrastructure and Systems
items.title: vLLM v0.32.0
items.summary: The release (814 commits) adds a /v1/systemone structured-decision endpoint and low-precision KV across hardware, including NVFP4 and 4-bit KV on ROCm. Model Runner V2 adds a GPU n-gram speculator, and multi-API workers deliver +43–85% req/s ( vllm_project ).

items.subsection: Inference Infrastructure and Systems
items.title: InferenceX accelerator benchmarks
items.summary: Inferact led a Google TPUv7 Kimi K3 (2.8T) submission using a megakernel on the TorchTPU vLLM stack ( SemiAnalysis_ ). TPUv7 vs GB300 : NVIDIA’s first GB300 FP4 counter-submission remains 1.64× worse in performance per dollar across most of the latency curve (…

items.subsection: Inference Infrastructure and Systems
items.title: SGLang megakernels
items.summary: SGLang merged megakernel support, approaching 1000 tok/s/user on GB300 NVL72 ( SemiAnalysis_ ).

items.summary: An independent Schlotzsky’s and Cinnabon franchisee cut menu repricing time by 95% and built a workflow that could free up $100K in cash flow.
